A documentation release: the README on
[crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/lazybw) now shows the logo, the demo and
the screenshots. lazybw itself is the same as in 1.2.1, which fixed several
security issues; if you are on 1.2.0 or older, update.

## Downloads

| File | For |
|---|---|
| `lazybw-1.2.2-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz` | any Linux on x86_64 (static binary) |
| `lazybw-1.2.2-aarch64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz` | any Linux on ARM64, including Termux on Android |
| `lazybw_1.2.2-1_amd64.deb`, `lazybw_1.2.2-1_arm64.deb` | Debian, Ubuntu and derivatives |
| `lazybw-1.2.2-1.x86_64.rpm`, `lazybw-1.2.2-1.aarch64.rpm` | Fedora, openSUSE, RHEL and derivatives |
| `lazybw-1.2.2-1-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst`, `lazybw-1.2.2-1-aarch64.pkg.tar.zst` | Arch Linux, Arch Linux ARM |
| `SHA256SUMS` | checksums of all of the above |

On Arch Linux it is also in the AUR, as `lazybw-bin` (this release's binary)
and `lazybw` (built from source).

The container image with `bw` included is on the GitHub Container Registry:

```sh
docker run -it --rm -v lazybw:/home/lazybw ghcr.io/syscallbrain/lazybw:1.2.2
```

lazybw needs the official Bitwarden CLI (`bw`) 2025.9.0 or newer. The
[user guide](https://syscallbrain.github.io/lazybw/) covers installation and
everything else.
